official_measurement_examples.name: 20 July 2026 programme update
official_measurement_examples.fact: HM Land Registry's programme page was updated on 20 July 2026 with further local-authority migration dates, so service coverage must be checked by authority and date.

official_measurement_examples.name: 22 July 2026 search-results update
official_measurement_examples.fact: The search-results guidance was updated on 22 July 2026 as Oldham joined the national register, illustrating that coverage changes over time.

official_measurement_examples.name: LLC versus CON29
official_measurement_examples.fact: Practice guide 79 states the national Local Land Charges search is distinct from CON29 enquiries, which continue to be answered by local authorities.

official_measurement_examples.name: Unregistered charge limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A local land charge can still affect a purchaser even if it was not registered; a search result must not be interpreted as proof that no unregistered charge exists.

official_measurement_examples.name: Spatial extent check
official_measurement_examples.fact: Official searches require the land extent to be identified and checked; an address or title-derived extent may need manual adjustment before the search is run.

official_measurement_examples.name: Originating authority role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Documents and detailed charge information are generally held by the originating authority, not necessarily HM Land Registry.

official_measurement_examples.name: Migration split
official_measurement_examples.fact: Where land crosses areas with different migration status, separate applications can be required to HM Land Registry and the relevant local authority.

official_measurement_examples.name: Charge is not development outcome
official_measurement_examples.fact: Local land charges may record planning conditions, listed buildings, TPOs and notices, but a charge record alone does not calculate parcel development capacity or resolve compliance.

core_rules: LLC search is distinct from CON29
national service coverage must be checked by authority and date
absence from a search is not absolute proof no unregistered charge exists
search geometry must match intended land extent
charge registration is not source-document interpretation
historic search results retain search time
migrated and non-migrated authority areas must not be treated alike
LLC record is not cadastral ownership proof
LLC record does not determine development yield
no parcel LLC clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
originating authority remains relevant for charge details and corrections
source_verification_note: Official HM Land Registry and GOV.UK sources checked on 2026-07-26; July 2026 migration and search-result updates retained with LLC/CON29, coverage and registration limitations; no parcel promotion.
